explain: Based on the parabolic diagram where 'b' is the rise and 'a' is the span, the slope/camber relation is expressed as 2b/a for the average gradient from edge to crown.

q: 2. Exceptional gradient in plains is .............
explain: Exceptional gradient is the steepest allowed for very short distances (max 100m). In plains, it is 1 in 15 (6.7%).

q: 3. A rising gradient of 1 in 50 meets a falling gradient of 1 in 500. The length of the vertical curve if the rate of change of gradient is 1% per 100 m .............
4. A valley curve is composed of just two transition curves without any circular curve in between to ...........
options: minimize the length of valley curve
minimize time of acting of down thrust on tyres
explain: Two transition curves meet at the bottom of a valley to ensure the comfort of passengers by minimizing the sudden impact of vertical centrifugal force (down thrust).

q: 5. Travel speed is .............
options: instantaneous speed of a vehicle at a cross-section
average speed of a vehicle crossing a particular cross-section
Distance covered / Time of travel excluding halting time
Distance covered / Time of travel including halting time
explain: Travel speed (or Journey speed) is the effective speed of a vehicle on a journey, calculated by dividing total distance by total time including delays.

q: 6. An advantage of 'one way traffic' system is .............
options: reduced number of points of conflicts
explain: One-way streets eliminate head-on conflicts and simplify intersections, drastically reducing the total number of conflict points.

q: 7. Pedestrian loading island is located in between .............
options: cycle lane and motor vehicle vane
explain: These islands provide a refuge for pedestrians and are typically placed where traffic streams diverge or merge.

q: 8. Rotary is ideally suited .............
options: when traffic is more than 4 streams join at the junction
when the pedestrian traffic is heavy
explain: Rotaries (roundabouts) work best when multiple roads (more than 4) meet at a single junction, as they eliminate complex signal phases and multiple crossing conflicts.

q: 9. An elliptical rotary island is provided when .............
options: most of the traffic is along its major axis
most of the traffic is along its minor axis
right turning traffic is more than 25%
traffic density is more than 3000 vehicles/h
explain: Elliptical shapes are used when the traffic flow is significantly higher in one direction (the major axis), providing more weaving length for those primary streams.

q: 10. An advantage of traffic signal is .............
explain: Traffic signals ensure the orderly flow of traffic by allocating right-of-way to different movements in a predictable, timed sequence.

q: 11. Thick white and black lines of 2 m to 4 m long provided along the width of a highway indicates ...........
explain: These longitudinal stripes (often called Zebra crossings) mark the legal area for pedestrians to cross the roadway.

q: 12. The width formation of a road means the width of .............
explain: Formation width is the finished top width of the embankment or the bottom width of a cutting, excluding side drains.

q: 13. The traffic carrying capacity of a single lane, depends on .............
explain: Lane capacity is influenced by vehicle speed and size, as well as external interruptions like intersections and railway crossings.

q: 14. In scanty rainfall regions, the camber provided will be .............
explain: Where rainfall is low, a flatter camber is sufficient for drainage and provides better safety and comfort for vehicles.

q: 15. On earth roads, the camber should preferably be .............
explain: Earthen roads are highly porous and susceptible to erosion, requiring a steep camber (5% to 6%) to shed water rapidly.

q: 16. The best compromise between the increase of the length of a highway and reduction in its load carrying capacity, is the ruling gradient .............
explain: 1 in 20 (5%) is often considered the ideal balance in hilly terrain, providing a decent gradient without significantly penalizing vehicle load capacity.

q: 17. Reduction of load capacity in a ruling gradient of .............
explain: A 1 in 20 gradient is estimated to reduce the effective load-carrying capacity of a standard commercial vehicle by approximately 10% compared to a flat road.

q: 18. If A is the projected area of a vehicle in square metres, V is speed of the vehicles in kilometers per hour and C is a constant, then the wind resistance R to the moving vehicles, is given by ...........
explain: Aerodynamic (wind) resistance is proportional to the square of the velocity ($V^2$) and the frontal area of the vehicle.

q: 19. If no super elevation is provided on a road along curves, pot holes may develop at .............
explain: Centrifugal force pushes the vehicle outward, increasing the pressure and wear on the outer edge of the pavement, leading to premature failure.

q: 20. The advantage of providing super-elevation on roads, is .............
options: reduced maintenance cost of the roads
explain: Super-elevation allows for higher safe speeds, which increases lane capacity (volume) and reduces lateral wear/tear on the pavement (maintenance).

q: 21. The width of the right of way, is influenced by
explain: Right of way includes the entire land area acquired for the road, including the formation, shoulders, and future expansion space based on road class.

q: 22. The type of transition curves generally provided on hill roads, is
explain: The spiral (clothoid) is the most commonly used transition curve on hill roads due to its superior comfort properties.

q: 23. A gradient along which the vehicle does not require any tractive effort to maintain a specified speed, is known as
explain: A floating gradient is one where the resistance to motion is exactly balanced by the descending component of the vehicle's weight.

q: 24. In complex situations, total time required for a driver to form a judgment and to act, may be taken as
explain: While standard reaction is 2.5s, complex urban or hazardous situations may require up to 3.0 seconds for full processing.

q: 25. Traffic census is carried out for
explain: A comprehensive traffic census captures volume, speed, and parking patterns to understand the overall demand on the infrastructure.

q: 26. If cross slope of a country is upto 10% the terrain is classified as
explain: According to IRC classifications, terrain with a cross-slope of 0-10% is 'Plain'.

q: 27. The desirable camber for straight roads with water bound macadam or gravel surface, is
explain: WBM surfaces are more porous and rough, requiring a steeper camber (3% to 4%) for effective drainage.

q: 28. While calculating the sight distances, the driver's eye above road surface, is assumed ............
explain: For design purposes (stopping and overtaking sight distances), the IRC specifies the height of the driver's eye level as 1.2 meters (120 cm) above the road surface.

q: 29. When a number of hair in bends are introduced, a minimum intervening distance in between is kept ............
explain: For hairpin bends in hill roads, the IRC recommends a minimum intervening straight distance of 20 meters between successive bends.

q: 30. The number of vehicles moving in a specified direction on a roadway that pass a given point during specified unit of time, is called ............
explain: Traffic volume is the number of vehicles crossing a section of road per unit time (e.g., vehicles per hour).

q: 31. Enoscope is used to determine ............
explain: An Enoscope is an L-shaped mirror box used for spot speed studies by observing the time taken by a vehicle to cross a short, known base length.

q: 32. The portion of a road surface, which is used by vehicular traffic, is known as ............
explain: The carriage-way (or pavement) is the specific portion of the road intended for the movement of vehicles, excluding shoulders.

q: 33. A camber consisting of two straight slopes joining at the centre is called ............
explain: A sloped camber consists of two linear planes meeting at the crown, creating a simple 'V' or roof shape.

q: 34. The rate of rise or fall of the road surface along its length, is called ............
explain: Gradient refers to the longitudinal slope of the road, representing the rise or fall per horizontal distance along the road's alignment.

q: 35. The stopping sight distance is always ............ overtaking sight distance.
explain: Stopping sight distance is the minimum distance required to stop, while Overtaking Sight Distance requires much more length to safely pass another vehicle.

q: 36. A curve whose radius gradually changes from an infinite value to a finite value or vice-versa for the purpose of giving easy change of direction of a road, if called a ............
explain: A transition curve (like a spiral) provides a gradual change in curvature, helping drivers introduce steering gradually and allowing for smooth superelevation runoff.

q: 37. A curve which consists of a single arc connecting ............
explain: A simple circular curve is a single arc of constant radius connecting two tangents.

q: 38. 'End of speed limit' is a ............
explain: This sign provides the driver with information about the road status rather than a specific warning or a strict command.
